utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has not yet taken the oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's quite right. Let the witness take the declaration. He's having trouble hearing. Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, the witness needs to be shown the witness identification sheet that we had prepared, and it should be in front of everyone here. No, not -- it has to be shown to the witness only.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the sheet, is there your name on the sheet, your birthday, and your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your ethnicity, your family status, and your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On the sheet, is there also the position that you had before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, this sheet needs to become an exhibit, and it has to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 354, to be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, in these proceedings you will be referred to by the code number C-061.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would need to go into private session for a period of approximately 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you interviewed as a suspect on several occasions in November last year and in January and February of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you explain how this contact with the Prosecution came about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, after I heard through the media that my name was on an indictment which the Tribunal had raised against Slobodan Milosevic, I asked through some organisations and individuals, people in Belgrade, to come into contact with The Hague Tribunal and especially with the representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor in order to clear up, first of all, my own role in the events that are mentioned and also for me to be able to say everything I know about those events. After that, I had contacts with representatives of the OTP. That's how it came about.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you believe that participating in a suspect interview would assist you in your own case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To clear up everything and to clear up the truth and, within the frameworks of that truth, my role in the events.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are you currently still under investigation by the Office of the Prosecutor in your own case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I have been informed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Are you aware that the military court in Split tried you and 18 other Croatian Serbs in absentia and convicted you to a prison term of 15 years for having committed the criminal act of imperilment of the territorial integrity of the Croatian state? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. I know about that. I know that it was prosecution for political crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would briefly show the witness the Exhibit 352, tab 169, the judgement -- the first-instance and appeal judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Where are we going to find this, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You'll find it -- it's Exhibit 352. That's the binder, the binder with the exhibits to be tendered through the witness. And it's tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't recollect giving exhibit numbers to these items. Did we do so on the last occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Remind me what they are, please. Perhaps the registrar would be kind enough to do it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Rule 92 bis is numbered Exhibit 351, the exhibit binder 352, the intercepts 353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the Exhibit 352, Your Honours, it's tab 169.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, if you briefly look at page 4 of the first-instance judgement, where it says --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: "Thus, the accused from 1 to 19 have committed the criminal act of imperilment of territorial integrity of the State, against the Republic of Croatia, punishable and defined under Article 236,b)cl.1.KZHR," and it gives the 15 years' imprisonment sentence. And I would also like you to look at the first page of the appeal judgement. That's the judgement of the Court in Zagreb. And it says here: "The appeals of the military prosecutor and the accused," and there come the list of names, "are rejected as groundless, and the judgement of the first-instance court is upheld."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, at that time when the first-instance judgement was adopted, did you know about it? Did you take part in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I heard about it later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you appeal the judgement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking of the investigation against you here in The Hague, are you aware that after the termination of the investigation against you, you may get indicted before this Tribunal for your personal conducts in the events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: After your arrival in The Hague, did you have several conversations with me and other members of the Prosecution staff in preparation of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the suspect interviews in Belgrade and your conversations here in The Hague, were you -- were any promises made to you regarding the outcome of the case against you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No promises were given me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were you granted any kind of immunity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was granted protective measures for testifying here, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were any promises made in case you would testify in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No promises were made.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think at this point in time I would like to give the witness a warning according to the Rule 90(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think that's appropriate. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: M. Babic, you should understand your position at the moment as a witness in the light of what we've been told about some of these interviews and the like and your position generally. You, as a witness, may object to any statement -- to making any statement which might tend to incriminate you. That means, of course, to admit or involve you in any criminal offence. If you make such an objection, it would be then a matter for the Trial Chamber to determine whether you should be compelled to answer the question or not. If you were compelled to answer and did answer under compulsion, the evidence which you gave as a result could not be used against you in any subsequent Prosecution for any offence except giving false testimony. That means, in effect, that you have the right to object to giving evidence about anything which you may think will incriminate you. It's a matter for you whether you do make such objection or not. We note, of course, that in your case the position is rather unusual because you have counsel here to represent you, but it's right that you should have the position formally explained to you so that you may know it. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, having heard the warning, what is your motivation to testify here in these proceedings? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to state in this trial the whole truth about the events that came to pass and what I know about and those that I took part in. Also, I consider that I do bear certain responsibility for everything that took place during that period of time in the territory of the former Yugoslavia, and I expect that my role will be assessed correctly both by the Prosecution and by the other institutions, if it comes to that, at this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I also expect that if it comes to that, that I be treated leniently.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Before the war -- I just want to go now through some of your positions you held before the war, and it's enough to just give yes or no answers because we go into more details later on. Before the war, had you been a member of the League of Communists in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you participate in the last Congress of the League of Communists of Croatia on December 1989 in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On this occasion, did the party in Croatia adopt the proposal to become independent from the League of Communists in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've got the microphone on. What is it, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was why is this a private session? The witness is a protected witness. We can't see his image. His voice is distorted. So why have a private session for these questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Why do we need one, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going now through the positions that this witness had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And they were so particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Very well, but let's do it as rapidly as we can, particularly if you propose to come back to it in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, the birth year in the summary is wrong, you recognise? The witness -- birth year of the witness, which is right?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What do you mean, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He was born - we are in private session - 1956 or --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It's 1956.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 1959 is wrong in the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: 1956 is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You haven't answered yet my last question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In February 1990, did you become a member of the Main Committee of the SDS party in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In April or May 1990, did you become the president of the Municipal Committee of the SDS for the municipality of Knin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you become, later on, the president of the Main Committee of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the Main Committee? The Regional Committee of the SDS of Krajina, for the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And how long did you remain in this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several months in the second half of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Besides your position in the SDS, did you become the president of the Knin municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About four years.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you become the president of the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you become the president of the Serbian National Council at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you become the president of the Executive Council of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in this position; from when to when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the 21st of December, 1990, up until the 30th of April, 1991. And the post was the temporary president of the Executive Council. And from the 30th of April, 1991, to the 29th of May, 1991, the president of the Executive Council of SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you at some point in time also become the president of the government of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. On the 29th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until December, the 19th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When the RSK was founded, were you its first president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how long were you in this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the 19th of December, 1991, until the 16th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In 1993, 1994, did you run against Milan Martic in the presidential election?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did take part in the elections for the post of president of the Republic of Srpska Krajina and Milan Martic was one of the candidates too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In 1994, did you get a position in the RSK government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I became Minister of Foreign Affairs in the government of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you, finally, become the president of the RSK again in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I became Prime Minister of the government of the RSK on the 27th of July, 1995, until the 5th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can go now into open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness a map. It's Exhibit 326, tab 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, the map has the title "The Republic of Serbian Krajina." Are you familiar with this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is this a map which has been exhibited, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, or not? I don't recollect it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's a new map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's have a copy, please. We seem only to have got one copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We turned them all over to the registrar. There should be one for each of Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We have it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the original -- do you have the original map with you, by chance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you provide this map to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the original map is of a better quality and would be more useful on the ELMO. I suggest that you allow the witness to use his map. It's exactly the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, if it goes onto the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You can use the map, sir, your map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the original map is actually two-sided, printed two-sided. On one side is the map as such, and on the back side are photos and a lot of text, describing what is to be seen on the map. And the translation of the map, you have -- you should have with you together with the map. And the translation goes on the map, on the first side from the left to the right, and the same for the back side.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, can we have the page with the landscape -- with the map, yes. Thank you. Witness, who produced this map? Do you know that? Does it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says on the back. I can't see very well. It was published by the military publishing, the military publishing company in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was that the military publishing company from the RSK or from the VJ, or another one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the VJ, the Army of Yugoslavia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And when was it produced? Does it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1994. I can't see very clearly. Just a moment. I noticed somewhere in the text that it said 1994, after the elections in the Krajina, the elections of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, on the page with the map, you -- can you again turn to the page with the map? You have there a map. Can we turn it so that the blue map in the middle is to be seen. Yes. Witness, in the middle of this map, there is the territorial distribution of Serbs by towns in Croatia according to the census of the 31st of March 1981, and the blue colour represents the Serbs. Is that what we see on this map, the percentage of Serbs in the region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was it similar in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Again on this page with the maps, in the right corner there is a map of Ustasha genocide against Serbian population in the territory of the Independent State of Croatia. That's in the right-hand corner. Why is it on this map? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This falls within a context in which mention of the genocide of the Serbian people during the Independent State of Croatia in World War II was mentioned. The context -- or rather, the message was that Serbs had to bear in mind what the Croatian Ustasha had done to them during World War II in order to avoid this being repeated in the armed conflicts that took place between 1990 and 1995 on the territory of Croatia and, according to this map, also on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, below this green map there is a blue box, and it gives certain data on the ethnic composition of Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja. Could you show us --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: First of all, can the map be folded differently, please. The map needs to show now -- yes. The map has to be opened.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, can you show us this region, the region of Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja? You have to move the map -- you have to move the map so that it can be seen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it says in the text, in the blue box, it says "Population: 135.800," and it says "95 per cent Serbs, 4 per cent Croats, and 1 per cent others." Do you know what these figures are, from which time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the assessment of the army in 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's at the right bottom side of the map. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But it's actually not necessary to put it on the ELMO. We want to look at the regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How was it in 1990 and 1991? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a question, if I may: Are you referring to the data in this table here or this table here?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm referring to the table in the right-hand corner of the map. The right-hand corner. Right. This blue box in the right-hand corner of the map, it says, for Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem and Baranja, it says 95 per cent Serbs, 4 per cent Croats, 1 per cent others. And my question was: How was it in 1991 -- in 1990 and 1991? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't found the information you're referring to, madam. Are you referring to Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going down, actually, through the blue box from the left-hand side down, and the first one is Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja. Do you have it now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I understand now. Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: My question was: How was the ethnic composition in 1990 and 1991 for that region? Do you know that? Approximately, not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the territory of Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja, the ethnic breakdown of the population was approximately half/half. Half Serbs, half Croats, and there were others as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now going down, Baranja -- Banija, sorry -- Banija, it says here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, it's not very clear to me because the box to which you refer on the map is not in English, so I expect we are to follow it from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have it only in this format. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the data which was just given comes under the heading "Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, and Baranja."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It doesn't seem to coincide with what is here, or is that for a different year? 1990 --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We are actually now comparing the situation in 1993, which is the situation marked on the map, and I'm asking the witness how it was in 1990, 1991, and he is giving these figures. It's not on the map. It's from his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We go now down to Banija, and on the map it says for 1993, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. population is 82.406, and the ethnic make-up is 97 per cent Serbs, 2 per cent Croats, and 1 per cent Others. And my question to you first is to show Banija on the map on the ELMO so that the Judges can see where it is, and then the ethnic composition in 1990 and 1991, if you know. The witness is pointing out the Banija region.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area of Banija.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And can you tell us what the ethnic composition was in 1990, 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 75 per cent was Serbs and the rest was other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And do you recall how many Croats lived there in 1990? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to a third, or 25 per cent to 30 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We go now further down to Kordun. Can you, first of all, show Kordun on the map, where it is situated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area of Kordun.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And on the map for Kordun for 1993, it says 98 per cent Serbs, 2 per cent Croats. Do you know how it was in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 75 to 80 per cent were Serbs and 20 per cent or so were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now going to Lika, can you show us where Lika is on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area of Lika.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In the map, it says for Lika 48.389 inhabitants and 90 per cent -- 93 per cent Serbs, 5 per cent Croats, 2 per cent Others. And can you tell us how it was in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1990, two-thirds or three-quarters were Serbs or, rather, 75 to 80 per cent were Serbs and 20 to 25 per cent were Croats and Others.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Going further down, Northern Dalmatia. Can you show us Northern Dalmatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the area of Northern Dalmatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It says on the map population 87.000, and ethnic make-up 90 per cent of Serbs and 10 per cent of Others. Can you tell us how it was in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 80 per cent were Serbs and 20 per cent Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When it says in the -- in the map it says 10 per cent of Others for Northern Dalmatia, does that mean Croats or who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the ethnic make-up of the population during the census in the area had Croats, Serbs, and those who declared themselves as Yugoslavs. And there was a smaller percentage of other ethnic groups. Less than 1 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, the last region is Western Slavonia, but we have already had a lot of evidence on Western Slavonia, so we do not need to talk about it now. Thank you. Would you now please turn around the map, because I would like to ask a few questions from the back side of this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On the map, Your Honours, when you go to the translation, page 3, there is a list of municipalities of the RSK, and it's actually 28 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you find the list of municipalities? Do you have it, sir? I would like to know just two questions. There is the municipality, under number 23, of Plaski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether I can see the numbers here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, there is actually the photo -- there is the photo. The photo is Knin, and below -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I found it. I found it. I found it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I just have a question in relation to number 23, Plaski. Plaski, when did it become a municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Recognised as a municipality and their representatives made part of the Assembly of Republika Srpska Krajina in December 1991. Before that time -- well, they became a municipality because first they were part of the municipality of Korenica, and they separated themselves from the municipality of Korenica in the autumn of 1991, and their delegation was part of the Assembly of the SAO Krajina in December 1991. So the exact time when they constituted themselves as a municipality and declared themselves a municipality I couldn't say, but it was before December or in late November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the town of Plaski, was it before then a part of the Ogulin municipality that was in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The town of Plaski and several surrounding villages were, in 1990, part of the municipality of Ogulin, but in early 1991 they held a referendum, and the town of Plaski and several villages around it with Serbian population joined the municipality of Korenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And my other question relates to number 26, the Serbian municipality of Zadar. The Serbia municipality of Zadar, when was it introduced and which villages belonged -- or towns belonged to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The former municipality of Zadar, which was a municipality in 1990, two Serbian towns, Donji Zemunik and Smokovic, held a referendum in early 1991 and joined the municipality of Benkovac. That was the situation in 1991. And then in 1992 or 1993, I'm not sure exactly when, the Serbian municipality of Zadar was constituted, but it was defined at the elections held in the Republic of Serbian Krajina in late 1991 as the Serbian municipality of Zadar, with one delegate in the Assembly of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. What the Serbian municipality of Zadar encompassed, what territory it covered, well, we could say part of the territory of the former municipality of Zadar which was under the control of Yugoslavia up to May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did it include the villages Skabrnja and Nadin? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In terms of territory, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And there is another text on this back side of the map. It's headed with the words "Republic of Serbian Krajina." And it actually gives a few features in relation to the regions we just talked about, and I have only a few questions related to that. For Northern Dalmatia, it says that Knin was the administrative centre. Was it so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it also says for Northern Dalmatia that it was relatively undeveloped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was it like this all the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I apologise. In answer to your previous question, Knin was not formerly the administrative centre of Northern Dalmatia but it was the main town. It was the centre of Northern Dalmatia in that sense. And in answer to your second question, yes, it was an underdeveloped area, as were the other parts of the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I have a question in relation to Banija. In Banija, there is mentioned the five municipalities: Petrinja, Glina, Kostajnica, Dvor na Uni and Caprag. The villages Dubica, Cerovljani, and Bacin, are they part of Kostajnica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is another article on the back side of the map, and it has the headline "How Republic of Serbian Krajina Emerged," and would you please find this. And as we are going through the details later on, I just have one question and it relates to the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's on page 9 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It says here: "In 1989, the Serbian people responded to increasingly aggressive Croatian chauvinism by establishing the Serbian Cultural Society 'Zora' in Kistanje, as well as by presenting a united front regarding national symbols and myths." When was this society established and what was the purpose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This society was first established in early July 1989, but it was formally recognised, legalised as the Serbian cultural association Zora in the autumn of 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who established this society?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was established by people who were of Serb ethnicity from the area of Knin, Benkovac, or, rather, Dalmatia and Lika. Jovan Opacic, from Knin, was the president of the society.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can now turn aside the exhibit. Witness, while you were still a member of the League of Communists of Croatia, did the Knin region have a particular reputation in the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, starting in February 1989 and July 1989 the League of Communists of Croatia, the then ruling party, was labelled as a centre of Serb nationalism because of the events that took place in February and June and July in the area of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What events had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In February 1989, during the strike of Albanian miners in the Trepca mine in Kosovo, there was political division around this event throughout Yugoslavia. The Croatian association of trade unions supported the miners' strike in Trepca, while at the same time a large rally was held in Belgrade in support of the policy of the Republic of Serbia in connection with the events in Trepca. In Knin, this gave rise to solidarity in the trade unions, in the large companies such as the nut and bolt factory. They supported the policy of Belgrade and they protested against the standpoint taken by the trade union centre in Zagreb which had expressed solidarity with the miners in Trepca.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. We do not need to have all the details, sir. Did anything happen in Kosovo Polje near Knin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The celebration of the anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo was held in that year in Kosovo Polje near Knin several days after the large celebration that was held in Kosovo Polje near Pristina. This was a ceremony in which many bishops of the Serbian Orthodox Church took part. It was a religious and cultural event, but at the end of the ceremony a political incident took place when Jovan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: M. Babic, as you'll appreciate, we've heard evidence about this from other witnesses. The significance, if I may say, as far as your evidence is concerned is any effect that it might have had in your region that you can speak of.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was what happened in Kosovo Polje near Knin understood in the Croatian society as a nationalist event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The representatives of the ruling party, the League of Communists of Croatia, and of the Croatian people, described this as a nationalist event.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why did you join the SDS party? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in view of the fact that I was following events surrounding the political position of the then ruling party in Croatia, that is the League of Communists of Croatia and its attitude towards Knin and the Knin Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. region, I was beginning to understand that a new party was needed to represent the special interests, the particular interests of that region. That is one of the reasons why I joined the SDS as a party which, in addition to the general democratic programme and reform of the society, had a special part of its platform related to improving the economic status of that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were the Serbs in Croatia in an unfavourable position in Croatia at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a fact that the municipalities with the majority Serb population in Croatia fell within the category of underdeveloped, economically underdeveloped regions. On the other hand, many Serbs realised that the former communist regime displayed a certain discrimination and suppressed the Serbs' linguistic identity in those areas of Croatia. Furthermore, at that time there was a media campaign to shed light on the position of the Serb people in Croatia which depicted their status as inferior and worse than the position of the majority Croat population.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This media campaign, who conducted this campaign? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That campaign was conducted by the state-owned media from Serbia, especially from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you attend the founding rally of the SDS in Knin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: When was it held and where was it held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 17th of February, 1990, on the square just above the railway station in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How many people attended and who was the president of the new party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was attended by 5.000 to 10.000 people, and a member of the Academy of Sciences, Dr. Jovan Raskovic, from Sibenik become president of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, for two questions I would like to go now into private session because it's the position of the witness in relation to this rally.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you give a speech on this rally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The offer was made to me to address the rally by the organiser, Jovan Opacic, and I did indeed make a brief speech, two or three minutes maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why were you offered to give a speech? At that time were you already heavily involved in politics, or why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was by chance that I was in contact with the initiators of the rally, Jovan Opacic and Marko Dobrijevic, regarding some premises they were looking for for the cultural society of Zora. I asked them how the preparations for the Assembly were going on, and on that occasion Jovan Opacic asked me, "Doctor, would you be willing to address the rally?" and I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Jovan Opacic --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I withdraw this question. We can do that in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What did you say during your speech? You said you gave a short speech. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was making that speech, I was under the impression of the things I saw while travelling from Zagreb to Knin when I was coming back from the party congress. I was thinking of the newspaper articles I was seeing at that time, especially in the Duga magazine, about the restoration of -- of the non-restoration of Serbian searches, et cetera, how people were moving out of Plitvice. And I remember that rally I said that the previous regime created a desert in the area from Karlovac to Knin. This was met with approval on the part of the members of the Assembly. And also, I supported the establishment of the SDS party as a party that would take care and represent the interests of the population of that area. And that is why I was offered to be on the Main Board of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can go now into open session again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You mentioned you and Opacic. What position did he have at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was president of the Serbian Cultural Society, named Zora, and one of the political leaders in the SDS, although he was not formally vice-president or anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did representatives from parties from Serbia attend the rally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many party representatives, and the main one among them was Kosta Cavoski, president of the Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were any members of Mr. Milosevic's party present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't familiar enough with those people.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milosevic support Jovan Raskovic politically? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, my impression then was that after the establishment of the SDS, and some time later perhaps, until the beginning of the war, the SDS did not enjoy the support of Belgrade, or rather, Mr. Milosevic. But after the beginning of the summer 1990, you could feel, at least in media coverage, that this support is there. Whether he supported Jovan Raskovic personally, I cannot say with any certainty, but I -- Jovan Raskovic did maintain contacts with then president of Serbia, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: While the SDS party was forming in Croatia, was there also a party led by Borislav Mikelic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There existed a wing in the League of Communists of Croatia led by Borislav Mikelic, and from that faction, Mikelic created the League of Communists of Croatia, which was pro-Yugoslav. That was in 1990, in the summer of 1990. It later sided with the group of leftist parties in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness now the SDS platform. It's the Exhibit 353, tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, is this the SDS platform from the 17th of February, 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've misspoken. It's Exhibit 351, not 353, and it's tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, looking at the first five pages of this document, does it refer to the opposition of the SDS party to the communist system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. This is the basic party platform at the time of the monopoly of the one ruling party, and speaks about the need for a multiparty system and a new economic system, on the basis of a multiparty system, and pluralism of ownership.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, how does it reflect opposition of the SDS party to the communist system?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are a lot of quotes in this platform, and I can read a few.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It would be better if the witness gave that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you refer us to the parts in this platform where it says that the SDS is in opposition to the Communist Party and wants democratic changes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, on page 1 -- it is leitmotif throughout the text, but you can see on page 1 the communist movement was historically defeated, and I quote: "Regardless of its sometime high rate of success, this movement suffered a historical debacle." And then it goes on to say: "This movement becomes the main obstacle for establishing political democratisation in our country. We believe that the way out of the crisis is not only economic and political, but also ethical, and lies in the creation of new parties and new movements. This is an idea that permeates the whole programme."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is one other --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So we could look through the entire text, if you think that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just one more quote in relation to that. It's actually -- in the English it's on page 4, in the second paragraph; in the B/C/S it's in a paragraph which starts with: "We are ready to cooperate with any party seeking a democratic way out of this situation. We are an opposition party, which is naturally inclined to other opposition parties, but we shall not accept to cooperate with any aggressive or repressive parties, especially not with those that advocate national egocentrism, hatred, and ethnic paranoia." Do you have this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember this. I remember this part very well. I just have to find it. You said page 4?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's in the English page 4, but it's actually two paragraphs after the last quote that you read, two paragraphs after the last quote that you actually read a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is page 2 in my text.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And I would like you now to move on to a paragraph that starts with the headline "System of government and the ethnic question." It is on page 4 in your text; and in the English, it's on page 8 and 9. Witness, it says in the first paragraph: "For the Serbian Democratic Party, the ethnic question is primarily a democratic question." And a few lines down it also refers to the unresolved ethnic question. What is meant with these references?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for the ethnic question in Croatia, it was believed that it was not resolved in a satisfactory manner as far as the Serb people are concerned, because the territories populated by Serbs were rearranged in the administrative division of Croatia. They were turned into parts of other municipalities and they became peripheral. It was further believed that this was the reason why these areas continued to be underdeveloped, were suffering from depopulation. And as a result, the Serb people were in an inferior position. They were linguistically neglected. Their media, education, and other areas of life and progress were not supported.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now I would like to refer you to page 6 in the B/C/S, and in English it's page 11. The headline "Democratic Federalism." It says here: "We believe that the fate of the Serbian people in Croatia depends on democratic federalism, hence we make our choice for a federative domestic organisation of Yugoslavia, under the conditions that it is accepted by all the constituent people of Yugoslavia." Does it mean in this chapter, "Democratic Federalism," does this chapter already refer to territorial autonomy within the federal units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in this paragraph perhaps, but it is mentioned in other paragraphs in other parts of the text. We see here there is an emphasis Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on the option for a model for organising Yugoslavia as a democratic federal state.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Does that mean Serb autonomy within Croatia? Did the SDS see Serb autonomy within the Croatian framework?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In other parts of this document, there are specific references to that. The Serb Democratic Party advocated a new administrative division of Croatia. It advocated territorial autonomy in those places where geographically, historically, economically, and for ethnic reasons, this was possible and even necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually in this paragraph. I refer you a little bit further down, where it says: "It is necessary to ensure constitutional possibilities to create territorial autonomies within individual federal units should the population in the territories with the special ethnic composition or cultural and historical identity so decide in a referendum." It's in that same paragraph. It's actually the last paragraph in this chapter.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Your Honour, it's on page 12, on the bottom, and in the beginning of page 13 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you find it, sir? It's page 7. It's the last paragraph before the next headline, Roman IV.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which number is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's page 7, the last chapter before the next headline. It's before this headline Roman IV, "Market economy."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We can assist with another copy here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you've got it marked on a copy. M. Babic, just look at that marked copy. Yes. Now perhaps you'd like to ask the question again, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, I just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I found it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I had asked you whether at that time you already had considered Serb autonomy within Croatia in certain regions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only in principle, nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did it mean cultural autonomy, more or less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could say that precisely it involved regional and local self-management, meaning territorial self-management, territorial autonomy, with local self-government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And if you move forward in the text, there is a -- there are listed the objectives of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Your Honours, it's on page 13 of this document. And we have marked it here. If the usher would just get it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, there is the objective 8: "Yugoslav democratic federalism must ensure constitutional possibilities within individual federal units so that territorial autonomies can be established should the population in the territories with specific ethnic composition or a special cultural and historical identity decide so in a referendum." Is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There is also the goal number 15, the objective number 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's on page 17 in the English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you have this? Witness, do you have it, or we have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. It says in this goal: "The recent one party politics brought us into an unacceptable situation. Certain parts of Croatia in which Serbs make up the majority of the population are economically backward and underdeveloped." And it continues a little bit further down: "The economic status of Serbs in those areas weakens, becoming even more unfavourable." That is what you actually have already mentioned, the dissatisfaction of the Serbs with their economic situation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in goal number 16, there is a reference to the regional division of Croatia. It says: "The regional division of Croatia is out of date and does not correspond to the modern principle of coexistence, and it particularly does not correspond with the historical interest of the Serbian people." Can you explain this? What is meant by this? Why was the regional division of Croatia against the historic interest of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is supposed to mean that the areas populated by Serbs, historically populated by Serbs as residents, found themselves on the periphery of administrative units, and that was the reason for their lagging behind in economic terms and for depopulation of these areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's now half past 10.00. We should come to -- is that a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because we would stay with this document another five minutes, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now. M. Babic, we're going to adjourn now for 20 minutes. Could you remember in this and any other adjournments that there may be not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Very well. 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness needs his microphone adjusted. Yes. Can you hear us all right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I forgot when we discussed the map that the witness had, I forgot to mention that this is a new exhibit. It was -- it gets now included into the exhibit binder, the Exhibit 326, the map binder. It's a new exhibit, and I have to tender it officially.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, while talking about the goal number 16, you mentioned the dissatisfaction with the regional division of Croatia and the disadvantage of the Serbian people. Was -- the regional division of Croatia, was that something that the new government, the Croatian government, had created or was it something that was in existence for quite some time before 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It existed before 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: So it was nothing new.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: A little bit further down in the document, there is the statute of the Serbian Democratic Party, and it starts in the English on page 20. And it's on page 12. It starts on page 12, sir, in the B/C/S. And there are just a few matters. It says in Article 6 that the Serbian Democratic Party is based in Knin. Was that decided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in Article 7, the party bodies are the Assembly, the Main Board, the regional boards, municipal and local boards, and party activists. Was that practised in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's how it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And there is an attachment to the platform, and it is the Serbian Democratic Party Resolution on Kosovo. It's the last two pages in the English, and it should also be the last page in the B/C/S. Why was this attached to the platform? What does Kosovo have to do with it, with the situation in Knin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Kosovo has to do with the overall political events on the territory of the former Yugoslavia, especially among the Serb people. In fact, the position of the Serbs in Kosovo as the public perceived it and learnt about it gave rise to national solidarity with their position, and of course the party saw the need to determine its own position therein.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That's enough for this exhibit. Witness, was the SDS then officially registered in Croatia and on the federal level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was officially registered both in Croatia and in the organs of the Croatian federation and in the Ministry of Justice of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to put to the witness just briefly the Exhibit 351, tab 2. And it is just to confirm the registration of the SDS party by the Croatian register of public organisations of -- as of 6 March 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. There's no need to discuss it. Did the SDS party take part in elections in Croatia, in the first election after the founding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did. The SDS did take part in the elections of the Sabor or the Assembly of the Republic of Croatia and the elections for the Municipal Assemblies in the area of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did the SDS win a majority in some municipalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In four of them, in fact, yes. Four municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Knin, Donji Lapac, Gracac, and Benkovac. In Benkovac there were additional elections, and it won those too.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In August 1990, was Jovan Raskovic opposed in the SDS after secret negotiations with President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In August 1990, was Jovan Raskovic opposed in the SDS party after secret negotiations with President Tudjman; and if so, who opposed him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At that time in the Main Board, a faction was formed against the president of the party, that is to say Dr. Raskovic, and this faction was led by Jovan Opacic, Dusan Zelenbaba, Branko Peric, and some other people as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Milosevic influenced this opposition? Did he have anything to do with this opposition against Raskovic and negotiations with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know whether Mr. Milosevic personally did take part, but the Belgrade press, at any rate, fanned the flames and instigated this lack of tolerance, especially towards Jovan Raskovic after his talks with Mr. Tudjman. And a journalist of Television Belgrade, on the eve of the SDS Main Committee meeting which was to have discussed some of these events, prepared a report in advance to the effect that the president of the party, the president of SDS, Jovan Raskovic, Dr. Jovan Raskovic, had already been replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But was he replaced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He hadn't yet been replaced. The group was a minority in the committee and later on, after one or two months, they stepped down from the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Mr. Raskovic eventually leave the region of Krajina; and where did he go, if so? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Raskovic left Sibenik for Belgrade upon the advice of academician Dobrica Cosic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was the SDS party meant to be restricted to the Krajina only or was it supposed to cover the whole of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serbian Democratic Party was founded with the object of covering the whole area of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. That is why it was formed in the first place and registered with the competent state authorities in Zagreb and with the organs in Belgrade as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was a party with that same name, SDS, founded in Bosnia in July 1990, and if so, who was the lead figure there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The name was similar. It was the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the president was Dr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Raskovic support Mr. Karadzic, and did they even campaign together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Raskovic did support Karadzic, and I heard from him that the election of Karadzic to a great extent took place because of the support lent him by Jovan Raskovic. So together they waged an electoral campaign. And Dr. Raskovic was very active in creating the Serbian Democratic Party in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there any dispute between Knin or Raskovic and the SDS of Bosnia and Herzegovina whether local SDS committees in the Bosanska Krajina around Banja Luka would associate with the SDS in Knin or the SDS in Sarajevo? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were such disputes and discussions about that between Raskovic and Karadzic or, rather, that was a conflict in the committees of the SDS in the area of Bosanska Krajina as to which party they would belong to, the SDS in Knin or the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And how were these conflicts solved? To which SDS party did those -- did this region then belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was solved in the following manner: All these committees belonged to the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina with its seat in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did Jovan Raskovic form regional SDS committees in Novi Sad and Belgrade; and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Committees were formed or, rather, Dr. Raskovic formed them at the beginning of the summer of 1990. He formed these committees in Belgrade and Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did they take part in election in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those committees, in the autumn of 1990, after the elections were called in Serbia, scheduled, these committees set themselves apart into a separate party, the Serbian Democratic Party of Serbia, and they did take part in the elections in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were attempts made to join the parties of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina at different times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which parties are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I was referring to the -- to the SDS parties in Croatia and Bosnia. And to assist you, I would like to put to you the Exhibit 351, tab 4. It is a public announcement by Krajina Serb Democratic Party regarding the talks with Republika Srpska SDS delegation of the 21st of July, 1993. And it refers in the text, in the first paragraph, to a visit of the RSK capital by the representatives of the state and party leadership of Republika Srpska, headed by President Radovan Karadzic, on the 19th of July. Do you recall, was there an attempt to join the parties or an initiative to join the parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me say beforehand that while Dr. Raskovic was alive, these -- this type of disintegration was taking place within the frameworks of the Serbian democratic parties, which means that independent autonomous SDS parties were set up in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbia, and Montenegro. After his death in August 1992, the Serbian democratic party of Krajina, of the Krajina, was set up. From the end of 1992 or, rather, the beginning of 1993, Radovan Karadzic led the initiative to have all these parties conjoined under his own leadership in Neum, or, rather, a party which would be called the Serbian Democratic Party of Serb Lands, of which he would be the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In this document, in the last paragraph, it says: "It has been concluded that the basis of the programme orientation must be the unity in achieving the Serb national interest." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unity in uniting the Serb peoples from the territory of the former Yugoslavia into one state.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it continues then in the document: "With the final achievement of that interest, the reasons for the existence of the Serb democratic parties in the republics would disappear, but, at the present stage of the fight for the preservation of the state sovereignty of both Republika Srpska Krajina and Republika Srpska, the existence of the parties on this level is unavoidable." Was that your position at that time, that you wanted to be separate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was our position, yes, while Dr. Karadzic's position was that the parties should unite.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We will now leave the parties and go to the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika. And I have a series of documents from Exhibit 351, and the first document is tab 5, and it's the stamped decision of the Knin Municipal Assembly dated 6 June 1990, approving an initiative to link the municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika. And the next document is the same exhibit, tab 6, and it is a draft statute of the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English translation, at least the version that I have, there is a mistake. It says "South Dalmatia," and it has to be "Northern Dalmatia." That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is this the statute, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document that came into being several months after the Association of the Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika came into being. This is a draft statute. And before this document, there were two other documents compiled. The first is the one we have here, the conclusion on the initiative to link up the municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika. And the second document is the document relating to the constitution of this association, dated the 27th of June, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And this one here, as I've already said, is a draft statute, which makes it the third document in line related to that particular topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Then we have to put now to the witness the Exhibit 351, tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's actually the document that you just mentioned, the Decision on Establishment and Constitution of the Regional Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika from the 27th of June 1990. That's what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it says here in Article 1, it says: "The regional association of municipalities of Northern Dalmacija and Lika also includes the municipalities of Knin, Benkovac, Gracac, Donji Lapac, Obrovac and Titova Korenica." Were these the municipalities that joined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, the municipalities of Knin, Donji Lapac, and Gracac, and later on the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. And coming back to this document, the draft statute, I would like to ask you something in relation to the introduction to the statute.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's on page 2 in the English, Your Honour, and this is the document tab 6 that we just briefly addressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It says here in this introduction: "The aim of this Statute is to legally sanction the current situation, that is, the established Association of the Municipalities of Northern Dalmacija [as read] and Lika, and the wish of the Serbian population in this area to introduce Serbian autonomy in Croatia." What was the reason to establish this association?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first reason to establish this association at the end of May and the beginning of June 1990 was to improve the economic position of the people to which this initiative referred in those municipalities, and the assertion of Knin as the headquarters and seat of this regional association, community; later on, once the Croatian Sabor, or parliament, or rather, the Presidency of the Republic of Croatia, launched the initiative for an amendment to the constitution of the Republic of Croatia and doing away with the possibility of creating an association of municipalities. The third reason and main political initiative taken to preserve this community and association was the one which had to do with preservation of national equality for the Serb people living in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In chapter 2 in this document - it's on page 3, Your Honours, in the English - and you can see the Roman chapter II here. And I quote here: "Regulatory competencies shall be listed by name. It is vital that they include rights and institutions connected with the use of the alphabet and the name of the language, schools and other educational and cultural institutions, reporting, religious freedom, and the appropriate institutions, as well as other concerns linked to the specific ethnic, historical, and cultural traits of the Serbian people." This association, did it basically refer to cultural autonomy and a certain regional autonomy within the framework of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like now to show the witness the Exhibit 351, tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is a letter dated 3rd July, 1990, from the Association of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika, to 17 municipalities, proposing a meeting on 6 July 1990, in Knin, of all municipalities with a significant number of Serbs, to adopt a unified position with regard to proposed amendments to the Croatian constitution. And my question to you is: Did such a meeting take place, and did you actually make proposals for the amendments to the Croatian constitution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meeting did take place and a large number of people took part, representatives of the municipalities and deputies in the Croatian Sabor of Serb ethnicity and other public figures, and views were put forward as to the proposed amendments, those proposed by the Presidency of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And now I would like to show you another exhibit, and this is Exhibit 351, tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it refers -- it is, actually, the declaration on the sovereignty and autonomy of the Serbian people, dated the 25th of July, 1990, and I would like to know from you who initiated the declaration on autonomy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The initiator to call this meeting and proclaim autonomy was Jovan Opacic, one of the leaders of the Serbian Democratic Party, and this initiative of his was taken up by the president of the party, Dr. Raskovic, and the others from the -- other members of the SDS. The declaration is the product of that initiative. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was there a particular reason to do that at this point in time, that is, the 25th of July, 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a specific reason. The Sabor parliament of the Republic of Croatia was in session; it was meeting. And on the agenda of the parliamentary meeting was the adoption of the new amendments to the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Croatia. And by those amendments, the possibility was wiped out for the existence of the association of municipalities. And the amendments introduced new symbols, state symbols for Croatia, a change in the name itself and the language. And the object of this was to hold the Sabor in Srb, with the appointed representatives of the Serb people in Croatia, elected ones, who would question the validity of the adoption of constitutional amendments along these lines, which would be taken by sidestepping the right to decide on the part of the Croatian people on a footing of equality with the -- the Serb Croat people on a footing of equality with the Croatian people. So these amendments would be brought into question and the majority vote would be taken by the Croatian people in the Croatian parliament, or Sabor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Who took part in the meeting in Srb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the meeting in Srb were the chosen representatives of the Municipal Assemblies, representatives in the parliament of the Republic of Croatia, representatives of political parties, representatives of the Serbian Orthodox Church, and about 100.000 citizens as well, from all parts of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did political officials from Serbia attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at the declaration in paragraph 1, in chapter 1 - it's on page 1 in the English, and it should also be the first page in the B/C/S - it says here: "In the process of establishing new relations in Yugoslavia, the Serbian nation in the Republic of Croatia is fully entitled to opt for a federate or confederate system of state government, either jointly with the Croatian nation or independently." What were the options that you had -- that you discussed at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the dominant options on the territory of the former Yugoslavia, as far as options to restructure Yugoslavia, were federal ones, the federal option, first and foremost, and the confederal option as well, for the new set-up of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It continues in this paragraph 1: "The Serbian nation claims a right to determine, on the historic territories united within the existing borders of Croatia, with whom it will co-exist, in what kind of regime it will live, and how it will relate to the other nations in Yugoslavia."
