utterances.text: To begin with, they got cash. I know that they got cash and technical equipment. Later on, they opened accounts. Later on, the Ministry of the Interior of Krajina had an account.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Why was the financing of the police not included in the SAO budget?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1991, there were no planned revenues and expenditures for the budget, but this was not the main reason. The main reason was the lack of funds. The SAO Krajina was only just being established. It consisted of an association of self-governing municipalities, and its revenue as very small. There was not enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: How was the TO financed at that time, Serbian TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until August 1991, employees in the municipal staffs of the Territorial Defence who had permanent jobs were paid by the municipalities. After the war broke out, the JNA entered the war and the TO joined in with the JNA, it was financed by the JNA. Later on, plans were made for the TO to have separate funding, but that was only from 1992 onwards. However, in 1991, for the most part, it was in the way I have just described.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would like to show the witness the Exhibit 352, tab 76. It is a specified request by Milan Martic to the Republic of Serbia, Ministry of Defence Belgrade, dated the 18th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, when you look at the header and the signature and the stamp, is that a genuine document? Can you comment on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is an authentic document. But I wish to mention that the stamp is not that of the TO Main Staff. It's that of the TO of the municipality of Knin. The other one is, I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, we couldn't hear the last half sentence that you spoke. It was too low in the tone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document is authentic, but the stamps used were those of the Territorial Defence Staff of the municipality of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature of Mr. Martic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is his usual signature, the signature I've seen on documents signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the other person, Savo Radulovic, who is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the Municipal Staff of the TO in Knin at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, without going into specifics, it's a request for several TOs such as Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, Vrginmost, Vojnic, in particular about -- at war Glina, in particular about ammunition and -- I think it's basically ammunition and equipment and weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, we are concerned about the time, as we mentioned before. I don't think you're anything like a quarter of the way through. We have got constraints of time, as you know, upon us, and therefore, the conclusion we come to is that the original estimate for this witness was, I think, 14 hours. We will give you a total of 16, which is four days. We said three, but we'll give you four, and could you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. please be through by then.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Much appreciated, and I'll do my best. I think it's going, actually, rather fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. M. Babic, will you be back tomorrow at 9.00, please, to continue your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
